# Cold-Chain Distribution Strategy: West & East African Corridors
## "One qualified cold chain, four corridor archetypes"

---

## 1. Diagnose correctly: this is four independent dials, not an equipment purchase

Most cold-chain designs start with "which box?" and then discover the box was never the binding constraint. Four things vary independently across African corridors, and conflating them produces either gold-plating on easy routes or silent loss on hard ones.

| Dial | What actually varies | Wrong response | Right response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thermal duty** | *Variance* in leg duration — customs dwell, breakdown, rainy-season reroute — far more than distance | Size the pack-out to the planned transit time | Size to **P95 duration + reserve**, qualified against the corridor's *hot-season* ambient profile |
| **Custody unit** ("what am I actually shipping?") | Node density, handoff count, session-site size, whether a district store exists at all | Ship pallets everywhere and let the ministry break bulk | Redefine the shipped unit per corridor: pallet, carton, **session-bundle** (one immunisation session, pre-picked), or CTC-eligible unrefrigerated last leg |
| **Institutional interface** | Customs predictability, MoH EVM score, who legally owns the vial at each point, last-mile staffing | "Hand over at the port and hope" | Set the **custody boundary deliberately** per corridor — and make it identical to the liability boundary |
| **Loss economics** | Product value per litre, freeze-sensitivity, replaceability, campaign vs. routine timing | Treat spoilage as an insurance line item | Underwrite on **cost per delivered *viable, documented* dose**, and only sell thermal warranty where you control custody |

**Core insight #1 — design against the tail, not the mean.** A Mombasa–Kisumu leg averaging 26 hours is irrelevant if its P95 is 71 hours because of a port dwell tail. Cold chains fail at the 95th percentile, and the 95th percentile is driven by *institutional* dwell (customs, document errors, ministry receiving hours) far more than by road quality. **Hours of unplanned dwell, not kilometres, is the design variable.**

**Core insight #2 — the dominant silent loss is freezing, not heating.** Across published cold-chain assessments, freeze excursions routinely affect a larger share of shipments than heat excursions, and they are far more damaging because they are **invisible**: a VVM (vaccine vial monitor) records cumulative heat, not cold. Frozen DTP-HepB-Hib, HPV, IPV, HepB and tetanus-containing products look perfect and are inert. The usual culprit is our own equipment — over-conditioned water-ice packs loaded straight from a freezer. **Any strategy that optimises only for heat is optimising for the less important failure mode.**

**Core insight #3 — for reusable passive shippers, reverse logistics dominates unit cost.** A $1,800 VIP+PCM shipper rated for 60 cycles costs $30/cycle at full recovery. But if each trip carries a loss probability of (1−*r*), expected life is min(60, 1/(1−*r*)) cycles:

| Recovery rate *r* | Expected cycles | Effective cost/cycle |
|---|---|---|
| 99% | 60 (rated life binds) | **$30** |
| 95% | 20 | **$90** |
| 90% | 10 | **$180** |
| 85% | 6.7 | **$270** |

Moving recovery from 85% → 97% cuts per-cycle cost ~8×. **The asset-return contract is a more powerful cost lever than the procurement negotiation.** This single number determines whether expensive high-performance passive kit is affordable on Sahel corridors.

**Core insight #4 — the commercial frame.** Do not price this contract per shipment or per kilometre. Price and manage it on:

```
CPDVD = Total corridor cost ÷ (Doses dispatched × Viability rate × Documentation-completeness rate)
```

Note the **two** multipliers in the denominator. A dose that arrives at 4°C but without an unbroken, auditable thermal record is, under most national regulatory authority (NRA) release rules, unusable. Data integrity is not overhead — it is part of the yield.

---

## 2. Global invariants vs. the corridor-configurable layer

Fix what defines safety and auditability; configure everything else.

**Invariants (identical on every corridor, no exceptions):**

1. **One qualified packaging catalogue.** Maximum six pack-out SKUs across the whole network. No field improvisation, no locally sourced coolers, no "we added a blanket."
2. **Release rule.** No dose is released to administration without a complete, verified thermal record plus intact VVM and freeze indicator. Absence of data = excursion.
3. **Custody boundary = liability boundary.** We never accept thermal liability at a node whose SOP, staffing, and equipment we do not control or formally audit.
4. **Freeze prevention ranks equal to heat prevention.** No water-ice in direct or indirect contact with freeze-sensitive product — PCM at +5°C only. Conditioning of any water-ice is a witnessed, timed, logged step.
5. **Every node is either power-redundant or a clocked pass-through.** A node with no SDD/ILR/generator backup is not a storage node; it is a transfer point with a hard maximum dwell timer.
6. **WHO PQS-prequalified equipment only** (or equivalently qualified and NRA-accepted) for refrigerators, freezers, carriers, and monitoring devices.
7. **One data spine, one alarm ladder, one temperature nomenclature** (+2–8°C / −20°C / −70°C / CTC ≤+40°C). Every device writes to the same record structure.
8. **Two seasonal pack-out qualifications per corridor** — hot-dry and wet — chamber-tested before go-live. A corridor is not live until both exist.

**Configurable per corridor (the "Corridor Profile"):**
Leg structure and staging depots; mode mix (reefer road / hybrid container / air / river / motorcycle carrier); pack-out selection from the catalogue; monitoring density tier; MoH handoff point; dispatch calendar and seasonal windows; buffer-stock levels; re-ice station placement; local partner mix; deposit/return mechanism for reusable assets.

**Rule:** a corridor gets a new *configuration*, never a new *component*. Any request for an out-of-catalogue pack-out goes to a qualification review gate — the same discipline that stops a fleet of 40 incompatible box types accumulating over three years.

---
